watchlist_events.title: CBRS: Cerebras IPO price watch and staged lock-up unlocks (2026-08-19)

metadata.note: User-supplied setup: watch Cerebras if price dips below $200, then especially if it tests the $185 IPO price. Current research source is the final 424B4 prospectus dated May 13, 2026, which confirms a staged lock-up schedule rather than a single August cliff. Revalidate current quote, borrow/options, earnings timing, and actual Form 144/insider flow before making any trading decision.
process: Price trigger 1: below $200, start full research refresh; do not buy only because the round-number level breaks.
Price trigger 2: near or below the $185 IPO price, look for capitulation, stabilization, and whether selling is event-driven or thesis-driven.
Buying rule: watch every tranche separately; a potential buy requires the unlock to fail to create a new low or to reclaim the broken level after the supply event.
If CBRS sells off before a tranche, wait 5-10 sessions after the unlock for no lower low, fading sell volume, or a reclaim of $185/$200 before considering a starter.
If CBRS holds up or rallies into a tranche, assume supply risk is not fully priced and avoid buying ahead of the event.
Lock-up: first fixed-date tranche is 2026-08-19 at 6:00 a.m. ET, up to about 14.6M shares.
Additional fixed tranches: 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-16 at about 14.6M shares each; 2026-09-30, 2026-10-14, and 2026-10-28 at about 19.4M shares each.

Earnings-triggered tranches: Q1 2026 earnings + second trading day released up to about 27.7M shares if the second-trading-day trigger was met, or about 30.2M if not; Q2 2026 earnings + second trading day releases about 36.4M shares.
Final remaining lock-up: earlier of Q3 2026 earnings + second trading day or 180 days after the May 13, 2026 prospectus date, which is 2026-11-09.
avoid: Treating August 19 as the final lock-up expiration.
Buying only because price is below $200 or below the $185 IPO price.
Ignoring Q2/Q3 earnings timing, Rule 144 limits, Form 144/insider filings, or underwriter lock-up release waivers.

metadata.note: User strategy 1: buy CPO and SiC names on major pullbacks. Core tickers are AAOI, LITE, SIVE.ST, and WOLF. AAOI/LITE/SIVE.ST are treated as the CPO/optical-interconnect basket; WOLF is tracked separately as a SiC turnaround/high-beta special situation.
process: Entry rule: do not buy the first red candle blindly; wait for a washout that stops making new lows, reclaims the prior breakdown level, or forms a higher low.
Starter size: 0.25%-0.5% per name or basket starter after the failed-breakdown signal; max basket size should be earned by evidence.
Core CPO names: AAOI, LITE, SIVE.ST; monitor adjacent optics/interconnect names COHR, CRDO, CIEN, MRVL, and AVGO for confirmation.
WOLF rule: keep smaller and separate from CPO; it is SiC/turnaround balance-sheet risk, not the same trade as optical interconnect.
Avoid adding if the group keeps making lower lows after earnings, if AI-infra tape weakens, or if the move is pure short squeeze with no fresh demand evidence.
avoid: Treating CPO and WOLF as the same risk bucket.
Averaging down before a failed breakdown, reclaim, or higher-low signal.
Letting a watchlist idea become a full-size position without written exit and capital source.

watchlist_events.title: SPACEX: SpaceX IPO opening and blowoff playbook (2026-06-12)

metadata.note: User strategy 2: play SpaceX IPO by participating in the low-float early move, selling into blowoff strength, then preparing a defined-risk bearish leg for lock-up supply and post-mania cooling. Current SEC source is the June 3, 2026 S-1/A, not a final 424B4.
process: First-day long rule: if participating at the open, use tiny tracking size with a hard maximum price/slippage limit; avoid an unlimited market order into a thin opening auction.
Sell rule: scale out into vertical/blowoff strength, opening-range exhaustion, or failure back through VWAP; do not let an IPO flip become an accidental investment.
Bearish leg rule: do not short the first-day squeeze. Wait for failed high, opening-range breakdown, options liquidity/borrow confirmation, or lock-up/event supply.
Preferred bearish instrument after liquidity exists: defined-risk puts or put spreads. Outright short only if borrow is available, costs are acceptable, and stop/recall risk is explicit.
RKLB proxy rule: use RKLB only if it is clearly trading as a SpaceX sympathy proxy; otherwise it is its own company risk.
avoid: Unlimited market orders on the first print.
Naked shorting low-float IPO strength before the tape breaks.
Using leveraged ETFs as a substitute for a clean SpaceX view unless holdings/exposure match the trade.

watchlist_events.title: SPACEX: SpaceX final prospectus and lock-up calendar rebuild (2026-06-12)

metadata.note: The June 3, 2026 S-1/A describes 180-day lock-up shares with timed automatic releases, plus a 366-day lock-up for Musk's shares. The actual calendar must be recalculated from the final prospectus date.
process: After final 424B4 posts, calculate 70, 90, 105, 120, 135, 180, 280, 340, and 366 days after the final prospectus date.
Track Q2 2026 earnings release as the first major release trigger: up to 20% of 180-day lock-up shares, plus another 10% if closing price is at least 30% above IPO price for five of ten trading days.
Track Q3 2026 earnings release and the 180-day backstop as the main post-mania supply window.
avoid: Treating June 3 preliminary S-1/A dates as final lock-up dates.
Building the put/short leg without the final release calendar.
